title.value: Halting Time is Predictable for Large Models: A Universality Property and Average-case Analysis
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Halting Time is Predictable for Large Models: A Universality Property and Average-case Analysis

extractions.description: The paper analyzes the halting time of first-order optimization methods for large-scale problems, revealing a universality property where the halting time is independent of the input distribution. It provides explicit average-case convergence rates and suggests this property holds for a broader class of algorithms and problems.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is about optimizing machine learning algorithms, and while potentially useful for sustainability applications, it is not a central theme.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Average-case analysis computes the complexity of an algorithm averaged over all possible inputs. Compared to worst-case analysis, it is more representative of the typical behavior of an algorithm, but remains largely unexplored in optimization.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on optimization algorithms in machine learning and does not directly address any specific climate or ecologically-related sustainable development category.
primary_category.quote: Traditional worst-case analysis of optimization algorithms provides complexity bounds for any input, no matter how unlikely. It gives convergence guarantees, but the bounds are not always representative of the typical runtime of an algorithm. In contrast, average-case analysis gives sharper runtime estimates when some or all of its inputs are random.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not directly relate to any specific climate or ecologically-related Sustainable Development sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: Yet, average-case analysis is rarely used in optimization because the complexity of algorithms is assumed to depend on the specific probability distribution of the inputs. Surprisingly, simulations reveal this is not the case for large-scale problems

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce any new category.
